## Growing peony  
China, Qing dynasty (1644- 1911), 18th century  Kei (silk tapestry), hanging scroll, 89.3 x 44 cm  Collector's seal: Lantang shuwu  Gift of Dr Lam Kwok Pun  HKUT.2008.1674  
This kei illustrates the different stages of the growth of a green peony. On the lower branches, three tiny flower buds are woven in red- coloured wefts. In the middle register the peony is blooming, and at the top it has fully bloomed. The gradation of tones on the peony and its leaves are finely woven with different shades of green- coloured wefts using the tanghansing (long- and- short propping) technique.  
Early kei were used as wrappers for Buddhist statues or for dressing tomb figures. The Song dynasty's (960- 1279) Huizong Emperor (r. 1100- 26) was thought to have encouraged the use of precious kei as wrappers for the imperial collection of painting and calligraphy. He favoured realistic bird- and- flower paintings, and kei weavers were encouraged to create tapestries depicting the beauty of the natural world.
